rules.title: Reject a window outside 1 to 90 days
rules.statement: If the window is missing, under 1 day, or over 90 days, the procedure raises LMS-031 and stops before reading loans. A window of 1 or of 90 is accepted. The as-of date is not checked by this guard.
rules.notes: The error text includes the rejected window value. There is no other validation of the inputs.

rules.title: Caller counts are discarded
rules.statement: Before any loan is read, the posted count and the skipped count are set to zero. Values supplied by the caller are not kept or added to, so both outputs describe only this execution.

rules.title: Only active floating-rate loans are read
rules.statement: The procedure selects loans whose status is exactly ACTIVE and whose rate type is exactly FLOATING, in loan-id order. Any other status or rate type is not read and is not counted as skipped or posted.
rules.notes: Matching is exact text. No other performing or non-performing classification is applied at selection.

rules.title: NPA loans are skipped and counted
rules.statement: If an otherwise selected loan has asset class exactly NPA, it gets no notice, the skipped count increases by one, and the procedure goes to the next loan. This happens before the missing-benchmark check, so an NPA loan with no benchmark does not stop the run.
rules.notes: Only the value NPA is tested. Any other asset class on an ACTIVE floating loan continues.

rules.title: A missing benchmark aborts the whole run
rules.statement: If a non-NPA selected loan has no benchmark code, the procedure raises LMS-005 and stops. It does not skip that loan or continue the loop. The procedure has no exception handler, so this error is not caught and later loans are not processed.
rules.notes: BEGIN at line 27 through END at line 78 contains no EXCEPTION section. Notices already inserted in the same caller transaction are not committed by this procedure.

rules.title: Reset date is the next cycle after elapsed whole months
rules.statement: Whole months from disbursement to the as-of date are the year part of the age times 12, plus the month part. Leftover days are ignored. That count is divided by the reset interval, the remainder is dropped, and one full interval is added. The result is stored in an integer. The reset date is the disbursement date plus that many calendar months. When the elapsed month count is already an exact multiple of the interval, that boundary is not used; the following interval is.
rules.notes: v_months is an integer (line 22). Remainder-dropping assumes reset_months is an integer; its column type is not in this file. No 30/360 or actual/365 day-count is applied, and no interest is accrued.

rules.title: Window is an inclusive calendar-day end with no start check
rules.statement: If the computed reset date is after the as-of date plus the window in calendar days, the loan is passed over and is not added to posted or skipped. A reset date equal to as-of plus the window is still eligible. Nothing requires the reset date to be on or after the as-of date. Days in the window are calendar days, so weekends and holidays count and are not removed.
rules.notes: Unlike the NPA and rate-change skips, this continue does not increment the skipped count.

rules.title: Saturday and Sunday notices move to Monday
rules.statement: The notice date is the reset date, except a Saturday is moved forward two days and a Sunday is moved forward one day, so both become Monday. Every other weekday is unchanged. No holiday table is read, so a public holiday is not moved.
rules.notes: PostgreSQL day-of-week 0 is Sunday and 6 is Saturday. The window test uses the unshifted reset date, so a Saturday on the last window day is still selected and the notice date falls two days after the window.

rules.title: Rates are latest benchmark plus spread, with gaps treated as zero
rules.statement: The new rate is the latest benchmark percent effective on or before the reset date, plus the loan spread. The previous rate is the latest benchmark percent effective on or before the prior cycle start, which is disbursement plus the computed month count minus one interval, plus the same spread. If no benchmark row qualifies, that part is 0, not missing. If spread is missing, it is 0. Both results are unconstrained numeric values and are never rounded.
rules.notes: v_old and v_new are declared numeric with no precision or scale on lines 25-26. There is no ROUND call. The same current spread is added to both rates, so it cancels in the comparison but remains in the posted amount.

rules.title: Moves under 0.25 are skipped
rules.statement: If the absolute difference between the new rate and the previous rate is strictly less than 0.25, no notice is posted and the loan is counted as skipped. A difference of exactly 0.25 is not skipped by this test. The comparison uses the computed numeric values with no rounding and no conversion to basis points. A loan that also already has a notice is still counted skipped only once.
rules.notes: Because a missing benchmark becomes 0, missing history can make the difference larger or smaller than the true benchmark move. The 0.25 test is OR-combined with the duplicate test.

rules.title: One notice per reset date is not posted again
rules.statement: If the loan already has a ledger row of type RESET_NOTICE whose note starts with the text 'reset ' followed by the reset date, no new notice is posted and the loan is counted as skipped. The match is that text prefix, not the rates. A prior notice for the same reset date blocks another even when the rates in the earlier note differ.
rules.notes: The date is turned into text, so the match depends on session date format. The note this procedure writes is built at line 75 as 'reset ', the reset date, ' from ', the old rate, ' to ', and the new rate.

rules.title: Posted amount is the new rate, and the loan is not updated
rules.statement: A loan that passes every check gets one ledger row of type RESET_NOTICE. The entry date is the weekday-adjusted notice date. The amount is the new rate, unrounded, not a currency amount and not the rate change. The note stores the original reset date and both rates. The loan record is not updated. The posted count then increases by one.
rules.notes: No accrual, bill, payment, fee, penal-interest, prepayment, or closure row is written, and no contractual rate on the loan is changed.

contradictions.description: The header calls this advance notice. The inserted entry date is the notice date from line 55, which is the reset date or the following Monday, never a date before the reset.
The 2015 comment fixes the horizon at the next 30 days. The code accepts any caller window from 1 to 90 days and applies that calendar-day horizon at lines 50-52. It does not hard-code 30.
The 2015 comment says the procedure lists resets. The code does not return a list. It inserts RESET_NOTICE ledger rows and only returns posted and skipped counts.
The 2019 comment says non-performing loans are skipped. The code skips only asset class exactly NPA. Every other asset class still proceeds when status is ACTIVE and rate type is FLOATING.

The header says the next reset must fall inside the window. The code only drops a reset strictly after as-of plus the window. It does not require the reset to be on or after as-of, and an out-of-window loan is not counted as skipped.

The comment says the rates are the benchmark on the reset date and at the cycle start. If no benchmark row is effective on or before the lookup date, the code substitutes 0, and a null spread is also 0, rather than failing or leaving the rate missing.

open_questions: Should asset classes other than NPA, such as SMA, also be excluded as non-performing, or is NPA-only correct?

When the as-of month count lands exactly on a reset interval, that reset is pushed a full cycle ahead. If the job misses the earlier window, that reset is never noticed. Is the lack of catch-up intended?
The window test has no lower bound. If the computed reset date is before the as-of date, a notice can still be posted. Should past resets be excluded?
A missing benchmark history becomes 0 instead of raising LMS-005. Should a gap fail that loan or the batch rather than skip or post against a zero rate?
A change of exactly 0.25 is notified; only a smaller absolute change is skipped. Confirm the cutoff is strictly under 0.25 and that rate_pct is stored in percentage points, not as a decimal fraction.
The same current spread is added to both rates, so a spread-only change never creates a notice, while the posted amount still includes spread. Are spread changes out of scope?
Duplicate blocking is a note-text prefix for that reset date, even if the rates differ, and it depends on session date format. Is once per reset date the intended key?
Only Saturday and Sunday move to Monday. Should bank holidays also move the notice date, and is a notice date after the look-ahead window acceptable?
reset_months is not checked for null, zero, or negative, and its type is not in this file. Should a bad interval skip the loan instead of aborting the batch on division or null dates?
The as-of date is not validated. Should a null as-of date be rejected before the loan loop?
Loans outside the window are in neither count. Should skipped mean only NPA, sub-0.25 moves, and duplicates, or every loan that did not get a notice?

This procedure does not change the loan's contractual rate and writes no accrual, bill, payment, fee, penal interest, prepayment, or closure entry. Confirm it is notice-only and another process applies the reset.
The ledger date is on or after the reset, not before it. Confirm that is the intended notice date rather than the as-of date or a date ahead of the reset.
